title: ee.peer_conflict.v1
description: Structured event row emitted by the SRR6.37 peer duplicate / near-duplicate / contradiction surfacer (bd-2w02i). One row per detection: an exact-content-hash duplicate, a near-duplicate candidate link, a contradiction candidate, a context pack that selected a memory under conflict, or a curation candidate whose promotion was blocked by a conflict. Captures conflict shape with provenance so `ee why` and `ee curate apply` can explain WHY they chose one memory over another (or refused to choose) without flattening peer disagreement into a single answer.

sideEffectFree.description: Conflict events describe a detection observation. They do not mutate the memory graph; a separate explicit `ee curate apply` call can act on them. The detector itself is read-only.

primaryMemoryHash.description: The memory whose presence triggered this detection (often a local memory or a recently cached peer memory). Hashed; raw memory ID never appears.

peerMemoryHashes.description: Other memories that participate in the conflict. Each is BLAKE3-hashed. For `duplicate_detected` this is the one identical peer memory; for `contradiction_candidate` it is the one peer memory that supplies the opposing claim; for `selected_with_conflict` it is every losing candidate in the pack assembly decision.

trustClasses.description: Trust class of each participating memory in the same order as the corresponding hash (primary first, then peers). Pin these per-row so a later replay can audit the trust-weighted detection without re-querying memory state.

nearDuplicateScore.description: When kind=near_duplicate_candidate: the SimHash hamming distance + cosine similarity between primary and the named peer. Absent on exact duplicates.

contradictionScore.description: When kind=contradiction_candidate: the deterministic score the contradiction detector assigned. The bead's first version uses conservative, deterministic heuristics; no LLM arbitration.

renderingPolicy.description: How the response surface (context pack / why / curate) should treat this conflict. The bead's acceptance text: `ee` should make these visible with provenance instead of flattening them into one answer.

conflictKind.description: Stable taxonomy of the four structured-log codes the bead acceptance names. Adding more is allowed in a minor revision; removing any breaks the consumer surfaces (`ee why`, `ee curate apply`, peer learn) that switch on these literals.

detectorVerdict.description: What the detector decided. `exact_duplicate` requires identical content hash; `near_duplicate` requires both SimHash hamming below cap AND cosine above floor (parallels embed-dedup); `contradiction` requires at least one of the contradictionScore.signal values; `co_present_with_conflict` is the conflict-surfacing case where the pack selected one but the row records the losers.

trustClass.description: Local trust class. Ordinary peer-origin material is capped at agent_assertion / agent_validated per ee.curate.peer_evidence.v1's trustCap rule. The dedicated signed active-member admission path may assign peer_human_attested; human_explicit remains strictly local.
